subject: Request: temporary reserved lanes + autoscale exception for NovaSearch pilot
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary reserved lanes + autoscale exception for NovaSearch pilot

Team —

Quick background: BrightDesk (pilot customer) is kicking off a 10-day performance evaluation for NovaSearch, their semantic search product. They will run heavy evaluation sweeps and latency-sensitive queries for the first week of June. The ask from Product/CS is for a short-term reserved lane with a controlled autoscale exception to ensure we meet the 99th percentile latency targets during the sweeps.

Proposal (high-level):
- Reserve an 8-GPU slice in us-west-dedicated-2 for 10 calendar days (start 2026-06-02, end 2026-06-11).
- Allow burst to 16 GPUs during nightly evaluation windows (00:00–06:00 PDT) via an autoscale exception rather than immediate pool-wide reallocation.
- Pin model to infer-v3.1 (canary was used in dev).

Why this route?
- The evaluation includes heavy cold-start workloads and KV cache prewarm steps that momentarily spike token throughput. Without temporary reserved capacity we risk degraded 99p latency and a failed pilot.

Asks for this thread:
1) Kimberly — approval from Product leadership to submit a temporary carve (policy exception) for a commercial pilot.
2) Jonas — feasibility + a short ops runbook for how we gate the burst (scheduling, soft-eviction thresholds, on-call playbook).
3) Marissa — confirm procurement path (MOU vs committed reserved) and whether we can include an explicit burst overage clause in the MAP.

Attachments: nova_requirements_v1.pdf (requirements), pilot_runbook.xlsx (schedule + test matrix), mutual_action_plan.docx (sales draft)

I’ll coordinate with BrightDesk (Aliyah) on exact test windows after we align internally.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary reserved lanes + autoscale exception for NovaSearch pilot

Thanks for the writeup, Aditya. A few quick clarifying notes before I sign off:

- Duration: can we confirm whether the 10 days are contiguous or if we can do a 7-day contiguous + 3-day follow-up (helps scheduling).
- Cost: we need an estimate of incremental cost (reserved + expected overage) so I can authorize the exception budget. Marissa — can you give an initial ballpark?
- Risk: if the burst spills into business hours we need an automatic fallback to a compatible, lower-cost model variant (e.g., infer-v3.0-quant). Jonas, please include fallback routing options in the ops plan.

Also please loop in CS lead for BrightDesk and FinOps if we land on >$XXk incremental spend. I’d rather keep this scoped and documented (MAP + a one-paragraph exec summary).

Kimberly Park
VP, Product

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-29T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary reserved lanes + autoscale exception for NovaSearch pilot

Heads up on capacity constraints and an ops suggestion.

Current state:
- us-west-dedicated-2 pool available headroom: ~12 GPUs across nodes (as of 2026-05-29 07:30 PDT).
- Existing scheduled commitments the week of Jun 1–7 have low utilization overnight but we cannot preempt production slices.

Feasibility + proposed control plane approach:
1) Reserve 8 GPUs as requested (we can carve from standby nodes) for 2026-06-02T00:00 to 2026-06-11T23:59. This is implementable but will require a soft-eviction grace on preemptible work and explicit tagging of the NovaSearch slice.
2) Autoscale exception: instead of instant pool-wide burst to 16 GPUs, implement a controlled ramp: allow burst windows 00:00–06:00 PDT and increase in 2-GPU increments every 10 minutes up to 16 GPUs. If latency registers >200ms beyond baseline or node saturation >85%, trigger rollback to 8 GPUs and notify on-call.
3) Fallback policy: route to infer-v3.0-quant if above thresholds for >5 minutes; record metric delta and open an immediate incident if service degradation persists.

Ops runbook notes (short):
- Preflight (48h): prewarm KV cache, run synthetic load tests on pinned canary.
- Nightly test window: telemetry dashboard watch, token-level tracing, cost meter.
- Escalation chain: infra on-call -> product on-call -> ops manager.

I attached a minimal runbook (pilot_runbook.xlsx) with ramp schedule and alert thresholds. If Marissa can confirm contract language and Kimberly signs the exception, I’ll schedule the carve and a 48h preflight.

—Jonas
Director, Capacity Allocations
jonas@redwood.ai

We will provide a MAP itemizing the days/times, telemetry expectations, and an overage clause for burst usage.

Action items for BrightDesk:

- Confirm you’re comfortable with an explicit burst overage charge rate (we’ll include an hourly overage cap in the MAP).
